Phrasal Verbs

A phrasal verb is a phrase formed with a verb + preposition.

The combination of the verb and preposition changes the meaning of the verb.
Here are some phrasal verbs related to work:

to work towards -- to take actions hoping to achieve a specific goal
to come up -- to think of
to go over -- to review, to study
to go along -- to accept, to agree to
to come in -- to enter
to go out -- to leave the house, to go to a place or places in the town or city
You conjugate phrasal verbs in the same way you conjugate other verbs.

Subject and Object Relative Clauses

When you want to make a complex sentence that has different clauses (phrases), you need to use a relative clause.

You can begin a relative clause with the relative pronoun who for people, which for things or that for either people or things.

You put the relative clause immediately after the noun it talks about.
A subject relative clause describes the subject of the clause.
An object relative clause describes the object of the clause.

Example 1:
The woman who lives next door to me brought me a cake.

The clause - who lives next door - refers to the woman.
Who lives next door? The woman
The relative pronoun who is used because you are talking about a person. It is also the subject of the clause.

Example 2:
The restaurant that we visited was near the center of the city.

The clause - that we visited - refers to the restaurant.
Restaurant is the object of the clause.
What did we visit? The restaurant.
The relative pronoun that is used because you need this information to understand the meaning of the sentence.

Example 3:
The price of food, which is very high, has gone up even more recently.

The clause - which is very high - refers to the food.
What is very high? The price of food.
The relative pronoun which is used because the information is not required for the meaning of the sentence.

images.text:
Welcome to restaurant management! We're sure this is a career that you will find very rewarding and enjoyable.

I wish I was always right, but in this business, it's the customer who is always right. Even if you don't agree with a customer's complaint, how you work through problems and come up with a solution will determine if the customer comes back to your restaurant. Restaurant managers must work towards this goal.

For a restaurant to run smoothly, it is important that each employee has an understanding of the role that has been assigned to them. The manager should go over every employee's role, and employees need to go along with how things are organized.

People who go out for the evening want to have a good time. They come in to your restaurant for a reason. If they don't know your restaurant, you need to give them one, like a special deal. Promotions can range from a nightly happy hour to prix fixe menus, to two-for-one dinner specials.

A restaurant menu should be updated regularly. The price of food changes and the cost of running a business changes as well. I wish food cost less, but it is very expensive. Restaurant menus have prices that keep food costs low and profits high.
